# Ankr

> Ankr runs blockchain infrastructure: JSON-RPC and WebSocket endpoints across many networks, indexed multichain data through the Advanced API, and Model Context Protocol servers that give AI agents read access to chain data with a management plane alongside them.

Endpoints take the shape `https://rpc.ankr.com/<chain>` for public access and `https://rpc.ankr.com/<chain>/<API_KEY>` for a project key. The canonical documentation is at https://www.ankr.com/docs/, and the pages below are the authoritative source for anything on this site. Where a marketing page and a docs page disagree, the docs page is correct.

## RPC and node access

- [RPC Service docs](https://www.ankr.com/docs/): endpoints, authentication, limits and errors.
- [Create a project and get a key](https://www.ankr.com/rpc/): the Web3 API platform, where keys and plans live.
- [Premium basics](https://www.ankr.com/docs/rpc-service/getting-started/basics-premium/): how a project key works.
- [Chains list](https://www.ankr.com/docs/rpc-service/chains/chains-list/): every network served, with its `<chain>` slug.
- [Service plans](https://www.ankr.com/docs/rpc-service/service-plans/) and [charging policy](https://www.ankr.com/docs/rpc-service/charging-policy/): rate limits and what calls cost.
- [Error reference](https://www.ankr.com/docs/rpc-service/errors/overview/): what a given error code from an endpoint means.

## Integrity and confidentiality

- [Verifiable RPC](https://www.ankr.com/web3-api/verifiable-rpc/): every JSON-RPC response is signed inside an Intel TDX enclave on the node; the open-source client SDK verifies the signature locally and fails closed, so an application can prove a response was not altered before acting on it.
- [Confidential RPC](https://www.ankr.com/web3-api/confidential-rpc/): a mode of Verifiable RPC that encrypts each JSON-RPC request and response end to end between the client SDK and one attested Intel TDX node, so Ankr routes and bills calls without reading their contents, and the node signs every answer. Enabled with one SDK option (`confidential: true`) or `vrpc-proxy --confidential`. Ankr still sees API key, client IP, chain, node, timing, sizes and status. Rolling out across Verifiable RPC chains; live in demo phase on the production network since October 2026; a dedicated confidential node is available on request.
- [Confidential mode docs](https://www.ankr.com/docs/verifiable-rpc/confidential-mode/) and [trust model](https://www.ankr.com/docs/verifiable-rpc/trust-model/): how to enable confidential mode and what each party sees, then what the attestation and signatures prove and which attacks they do and do not cover.

## For AI agents

- [Agent RPC MCP](https://www.ankr.com/docs/agentic-rpc/agent-rpc-mcp/): a hosted MCP server at `https://mcp.ankr.com/rpc` with twenty-five read-only tools, eight of them for Sui. Chain reads come back ABI-decoded and token-compressed. It authenticates with an Ankr API key in the `x-ankr-api-key` header, it cannot sign or broadcast anything, and it is also on npm as `@w3tech.io/agent-rpc-mcp` for running locally over stdio.
- [Management MCP](https://www.ankr.com/docs/rpc-service/getting-started/management-mcp/): a separate MCP server at `https://mcp.ankr.com/mcp` for keys, usage, balance and notifications. It signs in with OAuth in a browser; an RPC API key is not management authority there.
- [TORPC](https://www.ankr.com/docs/agentic-rpc/torpc/): the response-compression layer those tools rely on, requested with the `Accept-Token-Tier` header on ordinary JSON-RPC. The tier is negotiated per call and is not guaranteed, and every response reports the tier actually applied, though on a batch the reported tier is the lowest applied to any element, so a client reads each element from its own shape. The specification is at https://github.com/w3tech/torpc under CC0-1.0, with a reference implementation at https://github.com/w3tech/torpc-js under Apache-2.0.

## Data

- [Advanced API](https://www.ankr.com/docs/advanced-api/overview/): indexed multichain queries for balances, token holders, NFTs, logs and transfers, rather than per-chain RPC calls.

## Elsewhere on this site

- [Staking](https://www.ankr.com/staking/): liquid staking products.
- [Ankr Forge](https://www.ankr.com/docs/ankr-forge/overview/): the $ANKR rewards programs.
- [Changelog](https://www.ankr.com/docs/changelog/): what shipped, newest first.
